packageRules.description: Non-major updates merge themselves once the required checks pass

Every update waits until its release is 3 days old, so a broken or hijacked release has time to be pulled before it lands. With internalChecksFilter strict (Renovate's default, set here so it stays), Renovate creates no branch or PR for a younger release and lists it under Pending Status Checks on the Dependency Dashboard; once the age passes it opens the PR right away (prCreation stays immediate: not-pending would wait on checks that a PR-less branch never gets, since CI runs on pull requests), and non-major PRs automerge when the required checks pass
Pinning a digest keeps the release already in use, so it does not wait for the release age
Biome bumps change which code the lint and format checks accept, so they are reviewed by hand wherever Biome is pinned (package.json or mise.toml)

Our own image in deploy/compose.yml follows TELINHA_VERSION, which telinha-update writes, so Renovate neither pins nor bumps it. Today the variable in its tag already makes Renovate skip the line, and this rule keeps it out if the tag is ever written literally
LiveKit (client, server SDK, SFU) must move together and be tested by hand: own group, never automerged
The docs site's framework moves as one (Starlight pins its Astro peer) and Starlight is 0.x, so a minor can break the build; the docs CI job is not a required check, so the group is merged by hand
solid-js follows OpenTUI's exact peer and is never bumped alone; OpenTUI is 0.x so a minor can break, and the terminal smokes are not part of the required test job, so the group is merged by hand
Bumps in versions.json: the downloaded ones stay red until `bun scripts/versions.ts refresh`, the Caddy recipe needs the image job green; neither automerges or blocks the allNonMajor group
The SignPath action holds the signing token and returns the files that ship: pinned to a commit, every bump reviewed by hand

global.json's sdk.version is a floor, not a pin: rollForward latestFeature already uses the newest installed 10.0.x SDK, and raising the floor breaks tray builds on machines with an older SDK (10.0.300 locally), so a bump is a deliberate choice made by hand, kept out of the allNonMajor group

Bun is one version everywhere: mise.toml, packageManager, every @types/bun (pinned exactly, since a range lets bun.lock run ahead of the runtime), and the Dockerfile's oven/bun image. scripts/toolchain.test.ts fails while they differ, so they move in one PR, which waits for the last registry to publish
Go is one version in mise.toml and the Dockerfile's golang image, which builds Caddy; scripts/toolchain.test.ts fails while they differ, so they move in one PR

The Dockerfile (its golang and bun images too) and compose.yml ship in the image or the release tag, so their bumps must cut a release. A group PR takes its highest-priority type, so the bun and go groups are fix: whenever they carry the image
A digest-only refresh rebuilds the same image versions, so it is chore: and cuts no release on its own
versions.json pins the binaries baked into the image, so its bumps must cut a release
